content_units: Kickoff Agenda for 2026-02-12
Meeting:   Project kickoff
Time:     14:00–15:30 America/New York
Duration:     90 minutes
Participants:   Project manager, designer, frontend engineer, backend engineer, QA lead, marketing lead, client representative
Goals:   Align on scope, risks, timeline, and communication norms
A tight kickoff should confirm what is being built, how the team will work, what could go wrong, and what happens next.
90-Minute Kickoff Timeline
Phase   Goal   Key Tasks   Deliverable
14:00-14:10   Set context   Welcome; introductions; meeting goals; agenda review   Shared understanding of why the project exists and what this meeting will cover
14:10-14:25   Align on scope   Review business objective; in-scope items; out-of-scope items; success criteria   Agreed project scope and initial definition of success
14:25-14:40   Review users and solution approach   Discuss target users; key experience/design direction; product/technical approach   Early alignment on solution direction and major assumptions
14:40-14:55   Confirm delivery plan   Review milestones; dependencies; roles; decision owners   Draft timeline with owners and critical checkpoints
14:55-15:10   Surface risks and constraints   Identify top risks; note blockers; discuss technical, resourcing, approval, and timeline constraints   Prioritized risk list with mitigation owners
15:10-15:20   Set communication norms   Confirm meeting cadence; status format; tools; escalation path; approval workflow   Working agreement for communication and decision-making
15:20-15:30   Decisions and next steps   Recap decisions; assign actions; confirm immediate next milestones   Action list, owners, and near-term follow-up plan
Expected Outputs by Agenda Block
1) Welcome and framing
- Confirm attendee roles and decision-makers.
- Re-state the purpose of the project in one sentence.
- Outcome: everyone understands the objectives of the kickoff and their role in it.
2) Scope and success criteria
- Review project objectives, key deliverables, and known boundaries.
- Call out what is explicitly out of scope to avoid future drift.
- Outcome: documented scope alignment and success criteria the full team can reference.
3) User, design, and implementation alignment
- Designer shares intended user experience and assumptions.
- Frontend and backend engineers flag architecture or integration considerations.
- QA lead notes test strategy implications early.
- Outcome: shared view of the proposed solution and major feasibility assumptions.
4) Timeline, milestones, and ownership
- Walk through target milestones, review cycles, and dependencies.
- Confirm who owns delivery coordination, approvals, design handoff, engineering execution, QA signoff, marketing readiness, and client feedback.
- Outcome: initial timeline with clear owners and dependency awareness.
5) Risks and communication norms
- Identify top project risks across scope, timing, technology, approvals, and cross-team coordination.
- Agree on update cadence, communication channel, issue escalation path, and decision logging.
- Outcome: top risks captured and a team operating model agreed.
Pre-Read Packet to Send Before the Meeting
-   Project brief or statement of work
- Business goal, target audience, high-level deliverables, constraints
-   Draft scope outline
- In scope, out of scope, assumptions, open questions
-   Initial timeline or target launch date
- Key milestones, dependencies, approval points
-   Relevant discovery materials
- User research summary, stakeholder notes, prior project context, existing analytics if available
-   Technical context
- Known platform constraints, integrations, environments, security/compliance notes if relevant
-   Communication and governance draft
- Proposed meeting cadence, status reporting method, primary tools, decision owners
